newsitem.title: UK: UK to stay in EMU negotiations until end-Heseltine.
newsitem.headline: UK to stay in EMU negotiations until end-Heseltine.

text.p: UK deputy prime-minister Michael Heseltine said on Tuesday Britain would stay in negotiations over a single European currency right to the end.
"We will stay in the negotiations until the ink is dry," Heseltine told BBC Radio 4.
He said the government would not alter its "wait and see' policy on European and Monetary Union in the current parliament.
"We are not going to change our position in the election campaign or in this parliament," he said.
When asked if June would be the earliest the government's policy would be changed, Heseltine replied: "The very earliest."
The government must hold a general election by May 1997.

Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, the leading Europhile in the cabinet, had earlier on Monday dismissed a newspaper report that the government was reconsidering its wait-and-see stance towards a single currency.
Prime Minister John Major also dismissed the report on Tuesday as "fiction" and said nothing had changed in the government's stance.
